items.statement: Here a complex C$^*$-algebra is a complex Banach algebra with associative bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative norm, and a conjugate-linear involution satisfying $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$; **unital** means that it has a nonzero identity $I$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]]). A $*$-automorphism is a bijective complex-linear map preserving multiplication and involution. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a one-parameter group of such automorphisms, so $\alpha_0$ is the identity and $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$. It is **strongly continuous** when $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for each fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. A **state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$; this is the state convention of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]].

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4, pp. 74–75
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7, pp. 12–13

Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with free-boundary Hamiltonians $H_{\Lambda_n}$ on any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\Gamma$. Fix $\hbar>0$ and $\beta>0$, and let $\alpha_t$ be the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]].

items.title: Finite-range interacting quantum spin KMS existence
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement: Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, have finite on-site spin dimension $q\ge1$ and quasi-local spin algebra $\mathcal A$. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction with free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonians, and let $\alpha_t$ be the strongly continuous thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. Fix $\beta>0$ and $\hbar>0$. Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity, and the finite-matrix state/density-norm interface exactly as stated in Facts [A1]–[A2].
